depth.h2: What Ravenswood Homes Need From a Plumber
depth.intro: Ravenswood straddles the Lincoln Square and Uptown community areas. In Lincoln Square, the median home was built in 1944 and nearly half were built before 1940. About 1 in 3 homes there is in a building with two to four units. Here’s what that means for your plumbing.

tiles.title: Century-Old Sewer Lines and Drain Stacks
tiles.body: Homes from before 1940 often still have clay sewer lines and cast iron drain stacks. Clay lets roots in at the joints, and cast iron scales up and cracks along the seams. A [camera inspection](/chicago-ravenswood/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows the condition of your line before you decide on a [sewer repair](/chicago-ravenswood/sewer-repair).

tiles.title: Two-Flats: One Line, Two Homes
tiles.body: In a two-flat or three-flat, every unit drains into the same sewer line. A clog in the main line can back up into the lowest unit even when that unit did nothing wrong. Keeping the main line clear with regular [sewer rodding](/chicago-ravenswood/sewer-rodding) protects everyone in the building.

tiles.title: Heavy Rain and Basement Backups
tiles.body: In July 2011, record rainfall flooded basements across Ravenswood. Chicago’s sewers carry rainwater and wastewater in the same pipes, so a big storm can push water back into basements. A [backflow valve](/chicago-ravenswood/flood-control-maintenance) or an [overhead sewer](/chicago-ravenswood/overhead-sewer-systems) keeps it out.

tiles.title: Old Pipe, Low Pressure and Water Quality
tiles.body: Older homes can still have original galvanized steel water pipe, which rusts inside and slowly cuts water pressure. If you’re worried about what’s in your water, we can [test it and recommend a filter](/chicago-ravenswood/water-filtration-systems). If a pipe freezes and splits, we’re on call 24/7 for [burst pipe repair](/chicago-ravenswood/burst-pipe-repair).

items.q: How much does a plumber cost in Ravenswood?
items.a: It depends on the job. The main factors are what’s wrong, how hard it is to reach, the parts or materials needed and the age of your plumbing. Work on a century-old drain stack can take more time than a newer system. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins, so you know the cost going in.

items.q: I own a two-flat. Who’s responsible for the sewer line?
items.preview: As the owner, you’re responsible for your building’s sewer line and for keeping it clear.
items.a: As the owner, you’re responsible for your building’s sewer line and for keeping it clear. Every unit drains into it, so one blockage can affect the whole building. A camera inspection shows its condition and where any problem is.

items.q: Why is my water pressure so low?
items.preview: In older homes, the most common cause is galvanized steel water pipe that has rusted and narrowed inside.
items.a: In older homes, the most common cause is galvanized steel water pipe that has rusted and narrowed inside. A clogged aerator or a failing valve can do it too. We’ll check the fixtures first, then the pipes, and explain your options.

items.q: Do I need a water filter?
items.preview: Chicago’s water is treated and tested, but some homeowners want a filter for taste, peace of mind or protection for appliances.
items.a: Chicago’s water is treated and tested, but some homeowners want a filter for taste, peace of mind or protection for appliances. We can [test your water](/chicago-ravenswood/water-filtration-systems#water-testing) and recommend an under-sink or whole-house filter that fits your home.

items.q: How do I protect my basement from sewer backups?
items.preview: Start with a backflow valve on your sewer line and a regular check of the line for roots and debris.
items.a: Start with a backflow valve on your sewer line and a regular check of the line for roots and debris. For homes with repeat backups, an overhead sewer system lifts basement wastewater above the level where backups happen. We can look at your setup and tell you which option makes sense.
